evidence: The setup of the ALD-system is schematically shown in Fig. 1 a). ALD-growth proceeds by exposing the substrate surface alternatively to the different precursors. One growth cycle consists of (i) a pulse of the first gaseous precursor and its corresponding chemisorption onto the substrate, followed by an (ii) inert gas purge to remove the excess precursor. Subsequently, (iii) the second precursor is pulsed in and reacting on the surface to produce a monolayer of the desired material. Finally, another (iv) inert gas purge removes gaseous reaction by-products. In the present work, metal carrying precursors for the Al2O3 deposition are trimethylaluminum (TMA), and a chlorine-free tetrakis(diethylamino)zirconium Zr(NEt2)4 for the ZrO2 deposition, whereat the latter precursor has been kept at 110 °C. H2O has been used as oxygen-carrying precursor. The substrate temperatures during ALD growth have been set to 1 10 °C, 150 °C, 200 °C, 250 °C, and 300 °C, respectively. In order to achieve a reliable layer by layer growth, we applied purging times from 10 s to 90 s. Purge times have been kept short at high temperatures to avoid decomposition of the precursors and hence CVD-like growth behaviour. At lower temperatures, purge times have to be extended to remove the entire residuals from the substrate. In Table 1, the most important growth parameters and the related substrate-temperatures are enlisted. Three different dielectric stacks have been deposited: (i) 70 ALD-growth-cycles of pure ZrO2 (0/70/0), (ii) stacks composed of a 10 ALD-growth-cycles Al2O3 at the bottom and at the top of a 50 ALD-growth-cycles ZrO2, respectively (10/50/10), and (iii) stacks corresponding to 20 ALD-growth-cycles Al2O3 at the bottom and at the top of 40 ALD-growth-cycles ZrO2, respectively (20/40/20).
